items.title: Show HN: Try Vibe Robotics! (IRL or MuJoCo SIM)
items.description:
Show HN: Hey HN, I'm Salman, a research engineer at GDM Robotics on the team that built this robotics plugin. Whether you're a robotics founder, data company, making RL environments, or just getting FOMO seeing all the cool robotics demos on X, you can just plug in a robot and start prompting away. The plugin we've written up includes skills that steer the model toward following best practices. The benefits of using the plugin are: - fewer tokens (and therefore thinking time) needed to do bring-up the robot and to reach a successful attempt on your task - higher fidelity real-to-sim-to-real when creating MuJoCo assets and environments - leveraging strong motion planning, visual servoing, and collision avoidance We have tested on SO-101, YAM, and Franka Duo, but you don't even need real arms to test it out. You can just create cool environments in sim and then prompt the model to control a simulated robot in the environment! (Just make sure to tell it not to use privileged sim state if you want to actually evaluate how good the perception and model intelligence is). Just point your agent to the repo, good luck, and happy tinkering! Let me know if you have any questions! Will answer anything here or feel free to post on the GitHub repo directly.
Website metadata: GDM Robotics Skills for agentic robotics workflows across simulation and real robots. - google-deepmind/robotics-antigravity-plugin

items.title: Show HN: Archiver – free extract/compaction tool built with WebAssembly
items.description:
Show HN: I maintain a handful of archive libraries written in Rust and I had the crazy idea to throw them all together in a browser app, doing intense computational work, fully local in the browser. I've wanted to learn more about WebAssembly and this was a great opportunity to really see what it can do. Nothing is uploaded, there's no server behind it. Everything processes local and it even works offline and on mobile. I made a 7z on my phone in airplane mode today. There's a couple other tools like this out there, but they have sign-ups, ads, limitations. Archiver is a free tool for anyone and the only limits are what your disk can hold. For 7z specifically, it also picks the best compression filters for every file in the archive based on the file type, which is really powerful when you're archiving large, mixed data (text+pictures+binary) folders. Hope you enjoy.
Website metadata: Free archive tool in your browser. Extract ZIP, 7z, RAR, TAR, GZ and ISO, create encrypted ZIP and 7z archives, and repair with PAR2. No uploads or sign-up.

items.title: Show HN: Robotics needs better CAD, so I wrote a B-rep kernel and 3,487 tests
items.description:
Show HN: Hey HN, I’m Tony. I’m a co-founder of Springcraft, where we have been doing a lot of CAD modeling for robot parts. Our team kept running into limitations with existing kernels, and so I decided to write a new B-rep kernel and a new comprehensive, kernel-agnostic B-rep conformance test suite. Both are available today under MIT licenses. The kernel, springrep, is written in safe Rust with no dependencies. It covers a broad range of our mechanical CAD needs, including advanced fillets, sweeps, lofts, shells, offsets, STEP and exact measurements and queries. Claude Code made it feasible to write this, but it took a lot of time and care to get it right. The test suite, brep-conformance, has 3,487 cases covering the modeling operations common across kernels: booleans, fillets, chamfers, shells, offsets, sweeps, lofts, STEP, and queries with expected answers coming from closed forms and exact geometry. It caught hundreds of bugs, edge cases, and hot spots in springrep that our own tests had missed, and now springrep passes all of it. We’ve also run it on a few popular open-source kernels and anyone can run it on theirs. This is the first version, so there are surely mistakes in the test and adapters. Corrections, pull requests, and new kernels are welcome. kernel: https://github.com/springcraft-ai/springrep conformance suite: https://springcraft-ai.github.io/brep-conformance/
Website metadata: An open-source B-rep geometry kernel in safe Rust with zero dependencies, covering booleans, fillets, sweeps, STEP, and exact measurement. MIT licensed.

items.title: Show HN: Klistra – A complete studio for spec-driven AI motion design and video
items.description:
Show HN: As a solo-dev with a lot of projects going on, I found myself needing to make short promos or explainer videos. Not being familiar with animation software, I had the idea to use Claude to code up those videos and export them as video files. Note that this was before AI-coded music videos went viral, back in the early days when the models were just getting good enough to make the result actually look good. In the process of creating these clips I stumbled into a bunch of bugs and setup needed to make it work reliably. The list of features I wanted for better control and feedback kept growing and I needed to sign up for a bunch of services to get music, voiceovers and other media into my project. I couldn't find an existing service that had everything I wanted. Seeing these hurdles and that the technology was only easily accessible to people already confident with coding agents, I started working on Klistra, and a couple of months later I'm turning it into a service so you all can use it too. The goal with Klistra was to include everything I missed in the manual workflow into an easy to use service with a nice UI, so people could focus on what they wanted the video to look like, not setting up the framework behind it. Klistra includes precise timeline control, media generation, built in support to make animations match the rhythm of the background music, word extraction from voiceovers or songs, a dedicated iteration / feedback tool, web scraper and much more. Something I knew I needed to get right was making it easy to iterate on small features of the video with precise control of what was being built. I designed Klistra so you first create a specification where you define scenes in detail, describe what you want shown and when, reference media or timestamps in-line, freely drag the timeline around and preview the result before letting a builder agent create the video. If you want to change something, the specification changes and the builder agent gets a diff of what changed. This way there is always a written specification that matches the render / build. There is also a planner agent built into Klistra that helps create and edit the specification for you (which is what I use the most), while letting you turn to manual fine-tuning when needed. Don't think of this as a replacement for diffusion models, if you want photorealistic images or videos they clearly do a better job. Klistra really shines when you need motion design and precise control, exact text 
Website metadata: Describe it, add your files. Klistra plans it with you, then designs and animates it in every size.

We built a tool that lets you run the same test on your own website: https://assess.poh.org Enter your website URL, and we'll launch an AI agent to test your workflows, record its actions, and show how we evaluate the session. Below are three recorded tests. In the recorded tests below, agents were able to complete CAPTCHAs, bypass existing bot detection mechanisms, create and verify accounts, access gated resources, and carry out end-to-end workflows intended for humans.
